name: C01 trailingBlanks: back to the unanchored search
why: no answer changes, so cost tells it: the near-miss clock rows (a run in the middle, 50,000 blanks, 100 ms) and the six document rows at 100,000 blanks fail

name: C02 trailingBlanks: one character too few of the run
why: the enumerations and the fixed rows: the first blank of every run is lost

name: C03 trailingBlanks: one character too many
why: a text with no trailing blank answers its last character: the enumerations and the fixed rows

name: C04 trailingBlanks: the run ends where trimEnd() would (every Unicode space and line end)
why: a no-break space, a carriage return, a line feed and U+2028 end the text for trimEnd(), not for the search: the second and third enumerations and the fixed rows

name: C05 trailingBlanks: spaces only, a tab ends the run
why: the tab rows: the fixed rows, the enumerations and the behaviour rows with a tab gap

name: C06 trailingBlanks: answers the text WITHOUT the run
why: inverted: the fixed rows with a run, the enumerations and the behaviour rows with a gap (40 of the 58 rows of the file at Session 321's review round; the empty text and the rows that need no run still pass)

name: C07 trailingBlanks: the first run of blanks anywhere, not the one that ends the text
why: the reading the item's shape invites (a run before the pipe taken for the gap): the enumerations, the fixed rows with a run before the pipe, and the behaviour rows with blanks before the pipe

name: C08 trailingBlanks: a gap of at most one character
why: a two-blank gap becomes one: the mixed-run fixed row, the enumerations and the deeper-key behaviour rows

name: C09 trailingBlanks: a gap of at most 4,096 characters
why: a cap on the run (the obvious other cure for a quadratic): the near-miss row where the run is the gap itself (50,000 and 1,000,000) and the 200,000-blank row

name: C10 call site: the whole line, not the text before the key
why: the gap is the line's trailing run, which is empty: the deeper-key behaviour rows

name: C11 call site: the text up to the END of the key
why: the prefix ends in the key, so the gap is empty: the deeper-key behaviour rows

name: C12 call site: the text up to one column before the key
why: one blank of every gap is lost: a two-blank gap reads as one, so the deeper-key row finds a label it must skip

name: C13 call site: the RAW line, indent not taken off
why: the key slot counts from the stripped line, so in a list item the prefix is cut two columns early: the list-item deeper-key row

name: C14 call site: the text AFTER the key's start
why: the gap is the value's trailing blanks, empty: the deeper-key behaviour rows
